body.statement: Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\) and \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\).  Exact minimum-cost optimization over uniform certificates accepted by \(\operatorname{Acc}\) has a deterministic algorithm using at most \(2^m\) distinct queries to \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\), time \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\), and oracle-answer space \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\).  It returns the lexicographically first optimum certificate when \(\operatorname{Opt}<+\infty\), and otherwise certifies \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\).  Thus the first alternative in the oracle-search question holds; the bound does not assert a subexponential oracle lower bound or a compact scalar identifying functional.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(n=|V|\).  We give a finite algorithm, prove that its feasible objects are exactly the certificates accepted by \(\operatorname{Acc}\), and then bound its resources.

First enumerate the \(2^m\) protocol masks \(S\) in canonical order.  Membership in \(\Pi\) is decidable from Definition~\(\mathrm{Legal\ protocol\ class}\): count the SELECT actions, check the fresh-unit flag, the at-most-once mechanism condition, every precedence and conflict relation in the explicit catalogue, and CTF-REALIZE compatibility on \(G^{+}\).  All checks except the last are scans of the finite structural input.  The published CTF-REALIZE runtime lemma makes the last check polynomial in the encoded protocol and graph.  Query \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\) once for each legal mask and cache its immutable answer.  Thus no more than \(2^m\) distinct oracle queries are made.  A reply equal to \(\bot\), or a reply whose self-delimiting support index does not have the format in Definition~\(\mathrm{Certificate\mbox{-}independent\ physical\ input}\), supplies no candidate slice.

For each remaining protocol, enumerate the \(2^L\) masks \(\ell\).  Definition~\(\mathrm{Canonical\ literal\ and\ label\ encoding}\) decides by a finite scan whether \(\ell\) is consistent and uses only catalogued values.  The returned exact support table decides whether \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\) has positive mass.  Hence, by Definition~\(\mathrm{Measured\ source\ slice}\) and the positive-source-law assumption, precisely the well-typed positive slices that can occur in an accepted certificate survive.  Apply to each surviving slice the same ancestral-set transformation and bidirected-district decomposition used by the complete run.  There are at most \(n\) districts, hence at most \(n\) canonical single-district source factors \(T\) for this slice.  The measured-ancestry assumption and Definition~\(\mathrm{Measured\ source\ slice}\) decide and remove every source whose required transformed ancestors are neither READ nor fixed by a recorded action.  Every test so far is therefore both necessary for acceptance and exhaustive over protocol--slice--source triples that acceptance can use.

Fix a surviving triple \((S,\ell,T)\) and a target factor \(C_j\).  Enumerate the finite branch set \(\Omega_j\).  If the free request positions have domain sizes \(q_1,\ldots,q_r\), then the equality type is induced by the assignment and creates no independent choice.  Moreover,
\[
 |\Omega_j|=\prod_{h=1}^{r}q_h
 \leq \prod_{h=1}^{r}2^{q_h}
 =2^{\sum_{h=1}^{r}q_h}
 \leq 2^L.                                                    \tag{1}
\]
The first inequality uses \(q_h\leq 2^{q_h}\) for positive integers, and the last uses the fact that the canonical literal table has one distinct request literal for every allowed value at every such position.  For each branch, instantiate its value comparisons, construct \(D_T\) from Definition~\(\mathrm{Value\mbox{-}matching\ dependency\ graph}\), and run the deterministic ancestor--district recursion of the published IDENTIFY\({}^{+}\) recursion lemma.  On its stated connected, once-occurring factor inputs, Proposition~\(\mathrm{Connected\mbox{-}ancestor\ obstruction}\) equivalently declares failure exactly when \(\mathfrak O(T,C_j)\) is nonempty.  On success, Lemma~\(\mathrm{Fixed\ transcript\ size}\) supplies the canonical restriction trace, with at most \(|T|\leq n\) strict restrictions and \(O(n^2)\) bits apart from literal identifiers.  Its sets, districts, and value matches are checked by graph traversal and table comparison.

Replace the concrete values in each successful trace by their canonical request-position identifiers and compare the resulting finite strings.  By Definition~\(\mathrm{Uniform\ acquisition\ certificate}\), the triple admits a uniform transcript schema for \(C_j\) exactly when these canonical strings agree and the resulting schema verifies after substitution on every branch in \(\Omega_j\).  This is an exact finite test: necessity is the cross-branch verification clause in the definition, while sufficiency follows by substituting each enumerated branch into the common schema.  Let \(\mathcal W(S)\) be the resulting finite set of pairs consisting of a candidate record base \((\ell,T)\) and the set of factors for which that base has a verified uniform schema.  The construction is exhaustive; in particular, it does not interchange a pointwise existential source choice with the universal branch quantifier.

Form the finite local record universe \(\mathcal D(S)\).  For every \((\ell,T)\in\mathcal W(S)\) and every subset \(J\), possibly empty, of the factors certified by that base, \(\mathcal D(S)\) contains the canonical record with ownership mask \(J\) and the corresponding canonical transcripts.  Include also every syntactically permitted paid-protocol marker from Definition~\(\mathrm{Distinct\mbox{-}protocol\ cost}\).  Since \(k\leq L\),
\[
 |\mathcal D(S)|\leq (1+n2^L)2^k=2^{O(L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}).    \tag{2}
\]
Here \(k\leq L\) holds because each nonempty factor \(C_j\) contains a requested variable-value occurrence, giving at least one request literal with first coordinate \(j\), and different first coordinates index distinct literals.  Every record that can pass \(\operatorname{Acc}\) occurs in exactly one of these finite universes: its protocol, literal mask, extracted source mask, ownership mask, and verified canonical transcripts have all been enumerated.  Conversely, every enumerated record satisfies the corresponding record-local checks.  Define
\[
 w(S)=\sum_{a\in S}c(a),\qquad
 K(S)=\{j\in[k]:\text{some record in }\mathcal D(S)\text{ owns }j\}.             \tag{3}
\]
We next prove the central equivalence
\[
 \exists E\;\operatorname{Acc}(Q,E;G)=1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \exists\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi\quad
 \bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K(S)=[k].                             \tag{4}
\]
For the forward implication, every nonempty record of an accepted \(E\) passes the protocol, support, source-extraction, measured-ancestry, and cross-branch transcript checks in Definition~\(\mathrm{Operational\ acceptance}\).  Its owned \(j\) was therefore enumerated into \(K(S)\), and the ownership masks partition \([k]\); taking the distinct represented protocols proves the right-hand side.  Conversely, suppose the right-hand side holds.  Assign each \(j\) to the first protocol in \(\mathcal P\) that contains it in \(K(S)\), use the enumerated witness record for that factor, merge factors having the same record base, and sort the records lexicographically.  The resulting ownership masks partition \([k]\).  Every record passes the already checked legality, exact positive-support, source-extraction, measured-ancestry, and uniform transcript conditions.  The constructed full source list consequently presents a successful source to the exhaustive complete CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) search for every target factor, so that run does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).  All clauses of Definition~\(\mathrm{Operational\ acceptance}\) hold, proving the reverse implication.

Because costs are nonnegative binary rationals by the binary-rational-cost assumption, a minimum exists whenever the finite feasible family in (4) is nonempty.  Definition~\(\mathrm{Distinct\mbox{-}protocol\ cost}\) charges each represented protocol exactly once, independently of how many of its slices or records are used.  Thus (4) and Definition~\(\mathrm{Optimal\ acquisition\ cost}\) give the derived identity
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}
 =\min_{\mathcal P\subseteq\Pi:\,\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal P}K(S)=[k]}
       \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}w(S),                              \tag{5}
\]
where the minimum over the empty family is \(+\infty\).  Equation (5) is a consequence of acceptance and the cost definition, not a definition of the causal query or of identification.

List the candidate protocols as \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\), where \(p\leq2^m\).  For \(U\subseteq[k]\), set \(D_0(\varnothing)=0\), set \(D_0(U)=+\infty\) for nonempty \(U\), and use
\[
 D_i(U)=\min\left\{D_{i-1}(U),\ D_{i-1}(U\setminus K(S_i))+w(S_i)\right\}.       \tag{6}
\]
Induction on \(i\) proves that \(D_i(U)\) is the minimum cost of a subset of \(S_1,\ldots,S_i\) whose \(K\)-sets cover \(U\).  Indeed, an optimum either omits \(S_i\), giving the first term, or includes it, after which only \(U\setminus K(S_i)\) remains to be covered by earlier protocols, giving the second.  Thus \(D_p([k])\) equals (5).  If this state is infinite, (4) proves \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\), which is the promised infeasibility certificate.

When \(D_p([k])<+\infty\), recover the lexicographically first certificate by a finite self-reduction.  Let \(\mathcal D=\bigcup_i\mathcal D(S_i)\), ordered by the certificate encoding.  Its size is at most \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})\) by (2).  For any prescribed encoding prefix, decide whether it has an accepted completion of cost \(D_p([k])\) as follows.  The prefix forces some records, excludes every earlier incompatible record, fixes a set of already owned factors, and fixes the protocols already charged.  Reject it immediately if forced nonempty ownership masks intersect or a forced record fails its previously checked local conditions.  For each protocol, scan its remaining allowed records with the subset recurrence
\[
 A_{r+1}=A_r\cup\{U\cup J:U\in A_r,\ U\cap J=\varnothing\},                   \tag{7}
\]
where \(J\) is the next record's ownership mask and \(A_0=\{\varnothing\}\).  This computes exactly the ownership sets achievable by a locally valid subcollection: induction on the scanned records separates omission from inclusion, and the disjointness condition is precisely the ownership-partition requirement.  A second dynamic program over protocols and masks combines one achievable ownership set per protocol; it adds \(w(S)\) exactly when the protocol has not already been charged by a forced record.  Therefore the minimum returned by this constrained program is exactly the least cost of an accepted completion of the prefix.  Since (5) is the global minimum, such a completion of optimum cost exists exactly when the constrained minimum equals \(D_p([k])\).

Starting with the empty prefix, try the next encoding bit in lexicographic order and retain the first value passing this completion test, treating the self-delimiting end marker in the same way.  The invariant that the retained prefix has an optimum completion holds initially and is preserved by construction.  Finiteness of \(\mathcal D\) and of every record encoding makes the procedure terminate; at termination its output is accepted and has cost \(D_p([k])\).  If a lexicographically earlier optimum existed, its first differing bit would have passed the completion test and would have been chosen, a contradiction.  Hence the output is the lexicographically first optimum certificate, including the correct choice among any zero-cost, empty-ownership records.

It remains to bound resources.  Candidate generation performs at most
\[
 2^m\,2^L\,n k\,2^L
 =2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}})                 \tag{8}
\]
branch checks.  Recurrence (6) has \(p2^k\) updates.  Each constrained completion test uses at most \(|\mathcal D|2^k\) local updates and \(p3^k\) protocol-mask transitions; the bitwise self-reduction makes only a polynomial number in \(|\mathcal D|\) and the maximum record length of such tests.  By (2) and \(k\leq L\), all these quantities are \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\).  Exact addition and comparison of the input binary-rational costs have polynomial bit complexity per transition.  Every oracle payload inspected is counted in \(N_{\mathcal O}\); caching all replies uses \(O(N_{\mathcal O})\) bits.  Candidate masks, transcripts, predecessor data, and two dynamic-program layers use at most \(2^{O(m+L)}\operatorname{poly}(N_{\mathrm{in}}+N_{\mathcal O})\) bits.  Equations (1)--(8) therefore establish the stated query, time, and oracle-answer-space bounds.  The construction optimizes the explicitly restricted uniform-certificate acceptance predicate only; it neither outputs a scalar identifying functional nor asserts a subexponential oracle lower bound.
